  • Recording fee: Abstract or Torrens memorial $46 per document; $5 MN Conservation Fund fee on instruments with state deed tax or mortgage registration tax; checks payable to Hennepin County Recorder; fees per MN Stat. 357.18

Hennepin County by the numbers

Where does Hennepin County record a deed?

Deeds, mortgages, assignments, releases and satisfactions are recorded by the Hennepin County Recorder and Registrar of Titles on the 7th floor of the A-tower at the Government Center, 300 South 6th Street in Minneapolis. The same office also takes military separations and tax liens. The phone number is 612-348-5139 and the email is recordinginfo@hennepin.us.

Hennepin is Minnesota's largest county, with an estimated 1,284,784 residents in July 2025, and its recorder serves a county where roughly 45% of the land is registered as Torrens. That mix of abstract and Torrens parcels shapes how a sale gets recorded here, and it is the first thing to learn about a house you are selling.

How can I get a document recorded in Hennepin County?

There are four routes, and the county points different people to different ones.

  • In person by appointment, offered between 8:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. each business day. A walk-in is put on a wait list and helped when staff are free. Visitors pass security screening on the Skyway level first.
  • eRecording, which the county names as the preferred method for title companies, lenders, law firms and other commercial filers. Documents are recorded within 1 to 3 days, and the original never leaves your hands.
  • Online through the Virtual Recorder site, open to the general public. You register, build a package, and pay by card or eCheck. Each order carries a $3 service fee and is reviewed for recordability before you pay, then recorded in 1 to 3 business days.
  • By mail to County Recorder/Registrar of Titles, Attn: Document recording, 300 S Sixth St, MC 074, Minneapolis, MN 55487. The county returns originals within 1 to 2 weeks of receipt.

If a statutory deadline is close, call the office and ask which option fits.

What does it cost to record a deed in Hennepin County?

The standard charge for an abstract or Torrens document is $46, and a single check made out to Hennepin County Recorder can cover both the recording fee and any tax. The fees come from Minnesota Statutes 357.18. The schedule below lists the charges a seller or buyer is most likely to meet.

Selected Hennepin County recorder fees, from the county recording page
ItemFee
Abstract or Torrens document$46
Additional Torrens certificate$20 each
Assignment or satisfaction (abstract)$46, plus $10 for each reference over four
Well disclosure certificate$54
Conservation fee on taxed instruments$5
State tax lien release$30
Extra copies at filing$2

What taxes and paperwork go with a Hennepin County deed?

A transfer deed needs more than a signature. The county checklist asks for these items:

  • State deed tax, which the county states as .0034 of the net consideration, calculated with its online deed tax calculator. For a transfer of $3,000 or less the tax is $1.70, and the deed should carry the words "Total consideration for this transfer is $3,000 or less."
  • An electronic certificate of real estate value, or eCRV, with its number on the first page, for any deed over $3,000. Paper CRVs cause the package to be rejected.
  • A $5 agricultural conservation fee on any deed where state deed tax is due.
  • A "Send Tax Statements to" line with the name and address of every buyer.
  • A well statement or a well disclosure certificate with its $54 fee.
  • Grantor marital status, a full legal description, a drafter name and address, and a notary block with seal and commission expiration.

A mortgage carries mortgage registry tax at .0024 of the amount, and a contract for deed needs a well statement and an eCRV but no deed tax.

Does an unpaid tax bill stop a Hennepin County deed from being recorded?

Yes. The county checklist says properties with delinquent taxes may not be transferred, citing Minnesota Statutes 272.12. That section directs the auditor to check for delinquent tax, certify it, and mark the deed once it is paid or none is owed. The recorder cannot accept the deed without that mark, with exceptions the statute lists, such as deeds of distribution in probate and transfer on death deeds.

For a seller the practical step is to ask for the tax payoff before the closing date, so the title company can pay it from proceeds and the deed is not rejected. The property tax office at 612-348-3011 can quote what is owed on a parcel.

Why might Hennepin County reject a recording package?

County staff review a document only for the elements Minnesota law requires, so a package comes back when one is missing. Common reasons from the county checklist:

  • No date or signature, or an incomplete legal description.
  • No drafted-by statement with the drafter's name and address.
  • A notary acknowledgment missing the date, a legible seal, the signature or the commission expiration date. An individual acknowledgment also needs the signer's name and marital status, and a corporate one the business name and the signer's title.
  • Strikeouts, line throughs, whiteout, correction tape or staple removal on the original.
  • No eCRV number on page one of a deed over $3,000.

The office cannot supply forms, help fill them out or give legal advice. For that, the county points to Law Help MN, the Volunteer Lawyers Network and the district court self-help centers, and the Minnesota Department of Commerce keeps free templates meant to cut rejections.

Is my Hennepin County property Torrens or abstract?

Torrens land has been registered by order of the District Court or the Examiner of Titles, and it has a certificate of title that lists the owner, the legal description and every lien. The county says about 45% of Hennepin property is Torrens, and a new certificate is issued at each sale, in the way a car title is. Abstract property has no certificate, so an attorney or title company has to produce a report of owners and liens.

The property information search shows which kind a parcel is. An owner can get a free electronic copy of a deed or certificate of title by emailing recordsrequest@hennepin.us with the address or property identification number, and a Torrens owner can also call 612-348-5139 for a free copy.

What should a Hennepin County seller or buyer do after closing?

Recording is normally done by the attorney or title company, though the seller or buyer can do it. Once recorded, the county images and indexes the document, returns the original, and updates the taxpayer name and address from the deed. In most cases the document recorded first has priority.

Buyers can register the parcel with Property Watch, a free service that sends an email whenever a document is recorded against it. It does not prevent fraud, but it flags a recording nobody expected. If a joint owner has died, the survivor records an Affidavit of Survivorship with a certified death certificate. Owners who find an old racial covenant in the chain of title can discharge it, and for abstract property the county says there is no fee to record that disavowal.

More questions about Hennepin County, MN County Recorder

How much does the Hennepin County recorder charge for a deed?

$46 per abstract or Torrens document, plus a $5 conservation fee when state deed tax is paid, plus the deed tax itself. Checks go to Hennepin County Recorder, and one check can cover both fee and tax.

Can I record a deed online in Hennepin County without a title company?

Yes. The public can use the Virtual Recorder site after registering. Orders carry a $3 service fee, are checked for recordability before payment, and are recorded within 1 to 3 business days of payment.

How long does Hennepin County take to record mailed documents?

Originals mailed in are recorded and returned within 1 to 2 weeks of the county receiving them. eRecording from a vendor takes 1 to 3 days.

What is the Hennepin County deed tax rate?

The county's recording checklist gives the state deed tax as .0034 of net consideration, with a flat $1.70 when the price is $3,000 or less. Use the county's online calculator for the exact amount.

Where is the Hennepin County recorder's office?

It is on the 7th floor of the A-tower at the Hennepin County Government Center, 300 South 6th Street, Minneapolis, MN 55487. Call 612-348-5139 or write recordinginfo@hennepin.us.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Property documents accepted for recording only at the Property Taxation and Records office at the Administration Center in Hastings (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • RecordEASE online records: search fee $1 (subscriber $0.50), view recorded document $2 ($1.50 subscriber) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Dakota County?

Dakota County by the numbers

Where do you record a deed in Dakota County, Minnesota?

Deeds, mortgages and liens are recorded at the Property Taxation & Records office in the Administration Center at 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings. The county says documents are accepted for recording only at that office, either by appointment or by mail.

For questions call 651-438-4597 or write to records@co.dakota.mn.us. For a mailed filing, send the documents and fees to Attn: Document Recording, with a cover letter describing what is enclosed, a self-addressed stamped envelope and a phone number. Originals come back to the sender in one to two weeks.

What does recording cost in Dakota County?

Dakota County says every recording fee is set by the state, and that the $46 for indexing and recording a deed or other instrument comes from Minnesota Statutes section 357.18. That statute splits the $46 into $10.50 for the state general fund, $10 for the county technology fund and $25.50 for the county general fund. Fees are due when you file.

Dakota County recorder fees and transfer taxes (Property Taxation and Records filing fee page)
ItemAmount
Abstract document or Torrens memorial$46
Plat or registered land survey$56
Conservation fee$5
Well disclosure certificate$50
Extra copy submitted at filing$2
Deed taxPurchase price times .0033 (minimum $1.65)
Mortgage registration taxMortgage amount times .0023

Cash, check or card is accepted, and checks go to Dakota County Property Taxation & Records. A card adds a 2.49% service charge on recordings, none on copy requests.

What is the deed tax on a Dakota County sale?

The state deed tax is the purchase price multiplied by .0033, which is $330 on a $100,000 price and $1,188 on a $360,000 sale. Section 287.21 sets it at .0033 of the net consideration when the price, not counting liens that stay on the property, is above $3,000, and at $1.65 for $3,000 or less.

The tax is due when the deed is presented for recording. On a transfer worth $3,000 or less, the county asks you to enclose $1.65 and write "Total consideration for this transfer is $3,000 or less" on the deed. Above that amount an electronic certificate of real estate value is needed under section 272.115, and the certificate must be on file for the next homestead classification to apply.

What must a Dakota County deed contain to be accepted?

Dakota County follows the document standards in Minnesota Statutes section 507.093. Every document must be dated and signed, carry a complete notary acknowledgment, have the full legal description (not the tax description), attach any exhibits it references, and include a drafting statement and the filing fee. White-out is not accepted.

  • The deed tax is paid and the certificate of real estate value is complete.
  • The grantee's name and address are listed so future tax statements reach the right person.
  • Delinquent taxes are paid, and current taxes too if the parcel is being split.
  • A married seller is joined by the spouse, who signs and is acknowledged as grantor.
  • Well information is included: a certificate with the $50 fee, or one of the two statements the county prints on its recording page.
  • The $5 agricultural conservation fee is paid on transfers and mortgages.

A deed that completes a contract for deed needs a well statement signed by the buyers or a well certificate.

Why might the recorder return a Dakota County document?

The county lists the reasons it will send a document back unrecorded, and every one is avoidable with a check before you mail or bring it in.

  • Delinquent real estate tax is due on the parcel.
  • The drafting statement is missing.
  • The deed tax or mortgage registration tax is wrong.
  • The legal description is incorrect or looks questionable against county records.
  • The certificate of real estate value is missing or incomplete.
  • The mailing name and address for future tax statements is left out.
  • The notary acknowledgment is incomplete.
  • The recording fee is wrong, or well information is missing from a transfer.

Under section 272.12 the auditor must also confirm no delinquent tax exists, and the deed carries a note "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered" before the recorder can accept it. A correction document needs new signatures, new acknowledgments and a correction statement.

What is the difference between Abstract and Torrens land in Dakota County?

Minnesota has two land record systems. Most Dakota County property is Abstract, so a title company has to search the records for anything that touches the parcel when it sells. Torrens property has a Certificate of Title that serves as conclusive proof of ownership, with some exceptions, and the county charges more for Torrens work, such as $20 for each additional Torrens memorial, $46 for the first certificate canceled and issued on a transfer, and $40 for each additional certificate.

To see which system applies to a parcel, open the Property Information Search, enter the parcel ID or house number, and use the map layer icon. Owners can convert Abstract land to Torrens through land registration.

How big is the volume of transfers the Dakota County recorder handles?

The office keeps the property records for every parcel in a county of 185,931 housing units and 174,362 households. The Census Bureau counted 2,330 building permits there in 2025, and 89.0% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most addresses change hands slowly.

Dakota County was named for the Dakota bands, and the Treaty of Mendota in 1851 opened land here to settlement. Hastings, where recording happens, became the hub of the county by 1900 because of its position on the Mississippi, the St. Croix and the Vermillion River. The county seat stayed there even after the western suburbs boomed, which is why the Western and Northern Service Centers take tax payments but not recordings.

How can you search Dakota County records online?

The county's free Property Information Search shows tax, valuation and parcel data from a parcel ID, house number or address. RecordEASE is the paid tool for recorded documents, searched by legal description, grantor, grantee or document type.

Occasional users pay $5 a session, $1 per search and $2 to view a document. Subscribers pay $30 a month, $0.50 per search and $1.50 per document, and need an escrow account. Certificates of title cost $3 or $2.50 each. Veterans who recorded a discharge in the county can ask for a free DD214 copy, and most liens can be removed by filing a satisfaction, which stays on record as a permanent entry.

More questions about Dakota County, MN County Recorder

Can I record a Dakota County deed at the Western or Northern Service Center?

No. The county accepts property documents for recording only at the Property Taxation and Records office in the Administration Center in Hastings. You can also mail them to 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Dakota County?

The recording fee is $46 per document, plus the $5 conservation fee on transfers, the $50 well certificate if needed, and state deed tax of .0033 times the price. A card adds 2.49%.

Do I need a certificate of real estate value in Dakota County?

Yes, when the price is above $3,000, you complete an electronic certificate of real estate value. For $3,000 or less, none is needed, but you enclose $1.65 and add the required statement to the deed.

How long until the Dakota County recorder returns my original deed?

The county mails originals back to the submitter within one to two weeks. Include a self-addressed stamped envelope with a mailed filing. Questions go to 651-438-4597.

Does Dakota County help fill out a deed form?

No. The county does not help complete legal forms and takes no liability for people who do it themselves. Minnesota uniform conveyance forms are on the Department of Commerce site, so a seller who wants a deed drafted should ask a title company or attorney.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Carver County, MN County Recorder sale
  • Turn the Carver County, MN County Recorder offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Carver County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Carver County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Fees

Selling in Carver County?
We buy Carver County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Carver County by the numbers

Which Carver County office takes deeds for recording?

Deeds for Carver County land are recorded by the Land Records & Vitals office at 600 East 4th Street in Chaska, the county seat. Office hours run weekdays, 8:00am to 4:30pm, with closures on government holidays. Call (952) 361-1930 or write to recorders@carvercountymn.gov for land records questions.

The office handles more than deeds. Its own page lists conveyances, parcel splits and combinations, annexations, plats, mortgage registration tax, state deed tax, conservation fee collection and federal, state and county tax liens. Once a document is recorded it becomes a permanent record and cannot be changed or removed, so a seller who is about to sign should have the title company or an attorney check the deed first.

Staff will not hand you a blank deed or tell you how to fill one in. Blank forms come from the Minnesota Department of Commerce, which publishes the Uniform Conveyancing Forms.

What does the Carver County recorder look for on a deed?

The recorder checks a deed against a short list of items, and a missing one is the usual reason a document comes back. The county's recording requirements page names these for a deed:

  • A complete legal description. The shortened version printed on a tax statement does not count.
  • A full acknowledgment: the state and county where it was signed, the date, the notary's seal, signature and commission expiration date, and the marital status of each person acknowledged. A company signer needs the business name plus the signer's name and title.
  • A drafted-by statement with a name and address, and a send-tax-statement-to name and address.
  • A Certificate of Real Estate Value when the price is over $3,000.
  • Well information whenever an eCRV is filed, and a subsurface sewage treatment system disclosure on every transfer.

Paper deeds also need original signatures from the parties and the notary under Minn. Stat. 507.24. Correction fluid is banned. To fix a typo, strike the error with one line or a row of Xs, type the correction and have the parties initial it.

What fees come due when a Carver County deed is recorded?

Indexing and recording a deed carries a $46 statutory charge, set by Minn. Stat. 357.18. Of that, $10.50 goes to the state general fund, $10 to the county technology fund and $25.50 to the county general fund. Carver County's own page simply points to the statewide county fee schedule.

State law also bars counties from adding their own charges for handling, mailing, certifying that no delinquent taxes are owed, or collecting deed tax and the conservation fee (357.182). The line items that can appear on a Carver County deed closing are below.

Charges that can apply when a deed is recorded in Carver County
ItemAmountWhere it comes from
Recording fee, deed$46Minn. Stat. 357.18, subd. 1
Certified copy$10Minn. Stat. 357.18, subd. 1
State deed tax, sale over $3,0000.33% of net considerationMinn. Stat. 287.21
State deed tax, price $3,000 or less$1.65Minn. Stat. 287.21
Agriculture conservation fee$5 per transaction on a deed subject to taxCarver County recording requirements page
Well disclosure certificate$54Minn. Stat. 103I.235

How is Minnesota deed tax figured on a Carver County sale?

When the price is above $3,000, the deed tax is 0.0033 times the net consideration, which is the price without the value of any lien that stays on the property after the sale. A deed with no price or a price of $3,000 or less pays $1.65. The tax is due when the deed is handed in for recording.

For scale, the Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied home value of $453,600 in Carver County for 2020 to 2024. A sale at that figure with no lien remaining would carry deed tax of $1,496.88 (453,600 x 0.0033). The closing statement shows who covers it, so read that line before you sign.

Certain transfers are labeled designated transfers in the statute and pay only the $1.65 minimum. Ask your attorney whether a family or entity transfer fits that label before assuming it does.

What is the difference between Abstract and Torrens property in Carver County?

Minnesota keeps two land record systems, and the county says most Carver County parcels are Abstract property. Abstract land is proven through a title search of every recorded document that touches it. Torrens land has a Certificate of Title that serves as close to conclusive proof of ownership, and it folds the parcel's records into one document. An owner can convert Abstract land to Torrens through land registration.

Each system has its own recording rules, so tell the title company which kind of parcel you are selling. A document that covers both Abstract and Torrens land cannot be eRecorded at this time.

How long does recording take, and can the deed be eRecorded?

Under 357.182, a recordable instrument must be recorded, indexed and returned within ten business days. A county may take up to five more business days for documents that need a no-delinquent-tax certification or payment of deed tax, mortgage registry tax or the conservation fee. Electronically recorded instruments must come back within five business days of receipt in recordable form.

Carver County calls eRecording its preferred method and accepts nearly every Abstract or Torrens document type that way. Title companies, lenders and law firms sign up through one of the county's Trusted Submitters. A full eRecording also uses the electronic certificate of real estate value (eCRV) and the electronic well disclosure certificate (eWell).

What happens to the homestead status after a deed is recorded?

The certificate of value reaches the county auditor with the deed, then goes to the assessor and the Department of Revenue. Under Minn. Stat. 272.115, the assessor removes the homestead classification for the next assessment year on a sold property unless the buyer files a homestead application and qualifies. A parcel that needed a certificate of value cannot be classed as homestead unless one was filed.

Carver County's assessor (952-361-1960, assessment@carvercountymn.gov) handles homestead applications, and the county says a new owner, a trust transfer, a name change or an added or removed owner each calls for a new application.

What is the Carver County housing market like for a seller?

Carver County borders Hennepin County and belongs to the Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington metropolitan area. It is Minnesota's second-smallest county by land area, with 354 square miles, and the Minnesota River forms its southern edge. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 114,379 residents, up 7.0% from the 2020 base, and builders pulled 960 permits in 2025. The county's cities are Carver, Chanhassen, Chaska, Cologne, Hamburg, Mayer, New Germany, Norwood Young America, Victoria, Waconia and Watertown.

  • Median owner-occupied home value, 2020 to 2024: $453,600
  • Owner-occupied rate: 81.5%
  • Median household income: $125,946
  • Median gross rent: $1,514

Lake Waconia, at 2,996 acres, is the biggest lake in the county, and the eastern part of the county is dotted with smaller ones. A house with deferred repairs, a tenant or an inherited title follows the same recording steps as a move-in-ready listing. The deed, the certificate of value and the tax all go through the Chaska office.

More questions about Carver County, MN County Recorder

Where do I take a deed in Chaska?

It is the Land Records & Vitals office at 600 East 4th Street, Chaska, MN 55318. The office keeps weekday hours from 8:00am to 4:30pm and shuts for government holidays. Call (952) 361-1930 to reach it.

What does Carver County charge to file a deed?

The statutory fee is $46 for indexing and recording a deed. Add the $5 agriculture conservation fee on a taxable deed, the state deed tax and, where a well certificate is needed, the $54 well fee.

Does Carver County require a notary on a deed?

Yes. A paper deed needs original signatures and a complete acknowledgment that shows the venue, date, notary seal and signature, and the notary's commission expiration date. Electronic deeds follow the state's electronic recording standards.

Can a Carver County deed be recorded online?

Yes, for nearly all Abstract and Torrens documents, through one of the county's Trusted Submitters such as a title company. Documents that mix Abstract and Torrens land cannot be eRecorded yet.

Who pays the state deed tax?

The statute puts the tax on the deed presented for recording and does not say which party bears it. The sales contract and closing statement decide that, so ask the closing agent before you sign.

Anoka County by the numbers

Who records deeds in Anoka County?

The Anoka County Recorder and Registrar of Titles, part of Property Records & Taxation, files deeds, mortgages and satisfactions and keeps the permanent archive of recorded documents for real property. The office is at 2100 3rd Avenue, Anoka, MN 55303, and the number to call is 763-323-5400.

The Land Records & Recording page says the county does not give legal advice, help prepare documents or perform abstracting, citing Minnesota Statute 481.02. It tells people who need help to see a real estate attorney or a title company, and it takes no liability for people who complete documents themselves.

How much has Anoka County grown since 1960?

Anoka County went from 85,916 residents in the 1960 census to 363,887 in 2020, and Census Bureau estimates put it at 381,605 in July 2025. All of that population sits on 421.96 square miles of land, which works out to 862.4 people per square mile.

Geography shapes the records as well. The Mississippi River forms the southwestern edge and the Rum River crosses the western half. The southeastern tip that was once Manomin County joined Anoka County by constitutional amendment on November 2, 1869, and became Fridley in 1879, so very old deeds in that corner can carry unfamiliar place names.

  • 137,432 households averaging 2.67 people
  • 90.7% of residents unchanged in address over the previous twelve months
  • 69.6% of adults in the civilian labor force
  • 32.2% of adults 25 and older holding at least a bachelor's degree
  • Median owner cost of $686 a month for homes with no mortgage

Those are Census QuickFacts figures. Twenty cities share the county, including Blaine, Coon Rapids, Fridley, Andover and Ramsey, and parks such as Bunker Hills Regional Park and Coon Rapids Dam Regional Park sit among them. Every deed for a house in any of those cities is filed with this one county office.

What is the difference between Abstract and Torrens property in Anoka County?

Minnesota has two land record systems, and Anoka County uses both. Abstract property is the common kind, and the county says most property here falls into it. When Abstract property sells, a thorough title search should look for any document that mentions the parcel.

Torrens property has a Certificate of Title that gives conclusive proof of ownership, with some exceptions, and it pulls the record into one document. Owners may convert property from Abstract to Torrens through land registration. A seller who does not know which system applies can ask the recorder before the deed is drafted, because Torrens transfers carry their own certificate fees.

What must an Anoka County deed include to be recorded?

The county publishes a checklist on its recording requirements page. Go through it before you send anything.

  • The original document, dated and signed
  • A complete acknowledgment with the date, notary signature, legible seal and commission expiration date
  • Names and marital status of the people signing, and corporate details if a business signs
  • A complete legal description, with any exhibits noted and attached
  • A "Drafted by" line with name and address
  • Filing fees, with no white-out or white-out tape on any document
  • A "Send tax statements to" line naming the buyer
  • Payment in full of delinquent taxes, and of current-year taxes if the parcel is being split

Transfer deeds, including contracts for deed, also need a well disclosure. That can be a completed Well Disclosure Certificate with a $54 fee, or one of two sentences on the deed, either that the seller knows of no wells or that the well status has not changed since the last filed certificate.

What fees and taxes come due at recording in Anoka County?

Fees below took effect July 1, 2025 and come from the county's schedule. Deed tax is the large item, and it is set by Minnesota Statute 287.21.

Selected Anoka County recording charges from the fee schedule effective July 1, 2025
ChargeAmount
Recording fee for an Abstract document$46.00
State deed tax on consideration above $3,0000.33% of net consideration
State deed tax at $3,000 or less$1.65
Agricultural conservation fee$5.00
Well certificate$54.00
Mortgage registration tax0.23% of debt secured
Certified copy of a document$10.00
Interested party fee, per parcel$15.00

As an illustration, a sale at the county's Census median owned-home value of $346,500 would owe $1,143.45 in deed tax, plus the $5 conservation fee, the $46 recording fee and the $54 well certificate, for $1,248.45 before any other charge. The deed tax is due when the deed is presented for recording. Torrens filings have a separate fee list, such as $46 for a new Certificate of Title.

Mortgage paperwork has its own math. The mortgage registration tax is the amount of debt secured times 0.0023, plus the $5 conservation fee, and a mortgage paid in another county still owes the $5 in Anoka County. Satisfactions and assignments that cite four documents or fewer cost $46, with $10 more for each document cited beyond the fourth.

Do I need a certificate of real estate value in Anoka County?

Yes, for sales above $3,000, with a few exceptions. Minnesota Statute 272.115 requires the grantor, grantee or their agent to file a certificate of value when the deed is presented for recording. Anoka County asks for the completed electronic certificate, called an eCRV, and wants its number on the transfer document.

The certificate lists the sale price, the property's classification and the financing terms. It carries the Social Security or employer number of each party, which the statute treats as private data. A filed certificate also keeps the buyer eligible for homestead status, since the statute bars homestead treatment for a sold property when none was filed. The assessor removes homestead status for the following year after a sale unless the buyer applies and qualifies.

How can I submit a deed to the Anoka County Recorder?

There are three routes, and the county lists each one on its recording page:

  • eRecording, which title companies, lenders and law firms use, through submitters named by the county: CSC eRecording Solutions, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile.
  • Mail, with the documents and fees sent to Anoka County Property Records & Taxation at 2100 3rd Avenue, Anoka, MN 55303.
  • In person at the same address, paying by cash, check, debit or credit card, or Apple Pay.

If a title company is handling your closing, ask whether it will e-record the deed. If you are filing on your own, such as a transfer between relatives, send the signed original, the eCRV number, the well disclosure and a payment covering the deed tax and fees.

More questions about Anoka County, MN County Recorder

What is the recording fee for a deed in Anoka County?

It is $46.00 for an Abstract document under the schedule effective July 1, 2025. The state deed tax, the $5 agricultural conservation fee and a $54 well certificate fee come on top when they apply.

How much is the deed tax on an Anoka County sale?

It is 0.33% of net consideration when the price is above $3,000, and $1.65 when the price is $3,000 or less. The $5 conservation fee is added. The tax is due when the deed is presented for recording.

Does an Anoka County deed need well information?

Yes, every transfer deed and contract for deed does. Attach a Well Disclosure Certificate with its $54 fee, or put a qualifying statement on the deed that the seller knows of no wells or that the wells are unchanged.

Can I record an Anoka County deed online?

Yes, through eRecording submitters such as CSC eRecording Solutions, ePN, Indecomm or Simplifile. These services are meant for title companies, lenders and law firms, so an individual seller normally relies on the closing agent.

Will the Anoka County Recorder help me draft a deed?

No. The county says it does not provide legal advice, help preparing documents or abstracting, citing Statute 481.02. It recommends a real estate attorney or title company.
